description: Reframing gravity as an emergent swarm behavior: each particle follows simple local rules (attract neighbors, avoid collisions) that produce large-scale gravitational clustering. This inverts the usual perspective — instead of deriving behavior from a global force law, we ask: what minimal local rules produce gravity-like dynamics? This connects to artificial life and self-organization theory.
mathematical_formalization: Each agent i: a_i = sum_{j in N_i} [w_attract * (r_j - r_i)/|r_j - r_i| - w_repulse * (r_j - r_i)/|r_j - r_i|^3] + noise. With appropriate w_attract and w_repulse, the net effective force is ~1/r^2 at intermediate distances.
analogical_connections: Chemotaxis in bacteria: cells follow local chemical gradients, producing macroscopic aggregation
Ant colony optimization: local pheromone rules produce global shortest-path solutions
Market gravity models in economics: retail attracts customers proportional to size, inversely to distance squared
implementation_hypothesis: Agent-based model with attraction + short-range repulsion. Spatial hashing for neighbor queries. Tune parameters for stable orbiting clusters.
experiment_seed: Initialize 1000 agents randomly. Compare swarm rules vs Newtonian gravity: radial density profile, velocity dispersion, density fluctuation power spectrum.
